chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “When a man commits a sin, a black spot comes out in his heart. If he repents, it is erased; and if he increases, it increases until it overcomes his heart, and he will never succeed after that, ever.”

key_terms.انْمَحَتْ: it was erased or wiped away
key_terms.تَابَ: repented and turned back to Allah
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, the spiritual and moral center of the person
key_terms.نُكْتَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ: a black spot, meaning a dark spiritual stain caused by sin
key_terms.يُفْلِحُ: to prosper, succeed, or attain salvation

ai.seo_question: How do repeated sins affect the heart in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sin leaves a spiritual mark upon the heart, while tawbah removes that stain. Persisting in sin causes the darkness to grow until it dominates the heart and leads to lasting failure.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whenever the man sins a black dot appears in his heart. So if he repents, it is erased, and if he increases, it (also) increases until it overcomes upon his heart so he would not be successful after it, ever’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘When a man commits a sin a black dot appears in his heart. If he then repents, the dot will disappear, if he commits more sins it will increase until it will take over his heart and he then will never have salvation.’”
